== Synopsis ==

Alice's curiosity about a White Rabbit wearing a waistcoat and carrying a watch draws her into a peculiar sequence of transformations. Upon discovering a bottle labeled 'DRINK ME' on a glass table, she drinks from it and shrinks to ten inches high. After this initial shrinking, she realizes she has forgotten a golden key and cannot reach it on the table, though she does find a cake labeled 'EAT ME' beneath it. Her troubles multiply when she grows to nine feet tall, her body becoming disproportionately large and causing her great distress about managing her distant feet. She then slips and falls into a pool of tears she had created at her previous height, only to discover she is swimming in her own tears. When the White Rabbit appears dressed formally, he flees in terror at her attempt to speak with him, dropping his gloves and fan in his haste.

After falling into water, a wet party of animals and birds assembles on the bank, and Alice begins conversing with them as if she has known them her entire life. The Dodo declares that everybody has won and all must have prizes, then directs Alice to distribute comfits from her pocket as rewards. The Dodo later proposes a Caucus-race with no clear rules, where participants run when they like and stop when they like; after half an hour everyone is dry and the race ends. Alice discovers that pebbles thrown through a window transform into cakes, and she eats one to shrink back to a manageable size. In the Rabbit's room, she finds an unlabeled bottle and drinks from it, causing her to grow rapidly until she becomes trapped with her limbs protruding from the window and chimney. The Rabbit and other animals outside attempt to retrieve her, including sending a creature named Bill down the chimney, whom Alice kicks out violently.

After further shrinking, Alice finds herself with an extremely long neck, towering above the forest canopy and mistaking the treetops for green vegetation below. She breaks off pieces from opposite sides of a mushroom and tests them by eating small portions, experiencing rapid and disorienting size changes. Using the mushroom pieces carefully, she adjusts her size back to normal, then continues nibbling to reduce herself to nine inches before approaching a small house she discovers in a clearing. After an absurd conversation with the uncooperative Frog-Footman, Alice enters the kitchen where the Duchess nurses a baby amid excessive pepper smoke and chaos. She carries the baby outside and discovers it is gradually transforming into a pig, which she releases into the woods. Encountering the Cheshire Cat, she engages in philosophical banter about madness, and he mentions the Queen's croquet party.

Growing frustrated with the party's rudeness and illogical conversation, Alice leaves in disgust and discovers a door in a tree trunk. She re-enters the hall, uses the golden key to reach the garden, and eats the mushroom to shrink, finally arriving in the beautiful garden with flower-beds and fountains. The Dormouse tells a rambling story about three sisters named Elsie, Lacie, and Tillie who lived at the bottom of a treacle-well and learned to draw things beginning with M. Alice confides her frustrations about the game to the Cheshire Cat, who appears gradually in the air, while the Queen continues sentencing players to execution. Alice encounters three gardeners painting white roses red to hide their mistake before the Queen discovers it. When Alice defies the Queen's authority by refusing to lie flat during the procession and speaking boldly when questioned, the Queen orders her beheading.

Alice is escorted by the Queen back to the croquet game, where the Queen executes most of the other players except the King and Alice. The Mock Turtle begins recounting his past as a real turtle who attended school in the sea under a master called Tortoise and received an unusual education. The Queen asks if Alice has seen the Mock Turtle and offers to have him tell his history; Alice meets the Gryphon, who assures her the Queen never actually executes anyone. Alice recites a poem about an Owl and Panther sharing a pie, but the creatures grow frustrated with her inability to explain the absurdities. When the creatures demand Alice repeat lessons, she attempts to recite 'Tis the voice of the Sluggard' but it becomes 'Tis the voice of the Lobster' due to her distraction with the dance. Throughout these encounters, Alice observes the illogical conversations and strange customs of the underwater creatures with growing bewilderment.

During the trial, Alice experiences another growth episode and must negotiate space with the Dormouse sitting beside her. She observes the courtroom proceedings and notes the absurdity of the twelve jurors writing down their names before the trial has begun. The White Rabbit calls Alice as the next witness, to her complete surprise. She accidentally overturns the jury-box with her skirt, scattering the jurymen, and carefully retrieves them including the disoriented Lizard. Alice declares the court nothing but a pack of cards and defies the Queen's orders, causing the card-creatures to fly at her and disperse. She awakens on a riverbank beside her sister and recounts her dream; her sister later envisions the Wonderland creatures and reflects on Alice's future as a nurturing woman.
